anyio.verdict: Relevant conditional TLS-identity risk, not a demonstrated exploit in every consumer. Package-wide nonapplicability is not supported.
conditions: A non-ASCII certificate hostname reaches AnyIO TLSStream.wrap/connect_tcp without IDNA2008 pre-encoding.
The network connection is redirected or hijacked through another mechanism to a malicious peer with a certificate for the different IDNA2003 domain.

positiveCallerLeads.source: HTTPX0.28.1 URL normalization uses the idna package and hands an encoded ASCII host to HTTPcore; HTTPcore1.0.9 normally derives TLS server_hostname from origin.host decoded as ASCII.
positiveCallerLeads.qualification: This can control the ordinary HTTPX call path once exact installed versions/files/callers are bound. It does not cover direct AnyIO API calls or a custom non-ASCII sni_hostname extension.

verifiedUpstreamFix.mechanism: Resolve certificate hostnames through IDNA2008 before either standard or external SSLContext.wrap_bio. The upstream regression distinguishes sharp-s domain encoding and validates a legitimate certificate for the correct encoded name.

anyio.safeRemediation: Prefer a compatible Fedora-signed python3-anyio update/backport. The security commit is narrower than all changes between4.13 and4.14.2; test both SSLContext branches and current supported consumers. No pip overlay over RPM files.
anyio.owner: Fedora python-anyio maintainer / Bluefin; Finite qualifies signed package and supported consumers
anyio.unblockEvent: Approved owning RPM with this fix (or authenticated backport proof at actual shipped files), or complete positive consumer/hostname restrictions covering all supported calls. Existing package availability evidence is reused, not queried again.

rcloneCases.mechanism: Copying untrusted remote objects with --links can plant an escaping symlink and then write attacker data outside the destination as the desktop user.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported desktop client functionality; server exclusion cannot resolve this.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Reject escaping link targets in the owning-package fix; disabling --links would require an enforced, documented feature restriction, not an absent default flag.

rcloneCases.mechanism: SFTP remote hashing under PowerShell with SSH exec enabled interpolates attacker-controlled filenames; smart quotes can execute statements as the remote SSH account.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported SFTP workflow; Linux host proof alone is not nonapplicability because the command shell is remote.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Use fixed quoting for all PowerShell quote delimiters; disabling remote hashing/SSH exec can control this specific configuration but must cover every supported remote and cannot clear other rclone findings.

rcloneCases.mechanism: FTP/S3 serve/start receives request-local proxyOpt.AuthProxy but older constructors consult the unrelated process-global option. FTP can fall back to anonymous access; S3 with AuthKey can route authenticated keys to the fixed RC filesystem instead of the authorized backend.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported conditional server mode. Dedicated CLI-started servers are explicitly not affected by this option-scope mismatch. Anonymous S3 without AuthKey is not this advisory impact.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Construct each server from its own proxy options; validate FTP denial, authenticated S3 backend isolation and simultaneous distinct server configurations.

rcloneCases.mechanism: S3 auth-proxy without a separate shared signing secret can register arbitrary client access keys against an empty secret, so SigV4 authenticates no possession of credentials.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported conditional server mode; cannot call every rclone invocation exposed.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: The published newer source uses a per-identity-secret proxy flow, not merely the advisory illustrative startup guard. Existing S3 auth-proxy scripts and AuthKey semantics need migration and integration validation.

rcloneCases.mechanism: serve restic --private-repos authorizes one username prefix but passes an uncanonicalized path to backends; parent components can select another user repository.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported conditional server mode with path-normalizing backends, including memory/SFTP/FTP; append-only does not prevent cross-tenant reads.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Reject dot/parent components before both authorization and backend object selection; exercise read/write/delete and private repository separation against supported backend families.

rcloneCases.mechanism: serve restic accepts leading ../ paths on affected backends, exposing objects outside the configured root.
rcloneCases.verdict: Relevant supported conditional server mode; the publisher confirms multiple backend manifestations rather than only WebDAV.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Use the fixed canonical relative-path validation (io/fs.ValidPath plus rejection of dot root); validate root confinement across supported backends and methods.

rcloneCases.mechanism: A username-global credential map can replace an existing session credential after another login. The publisher confirms v1.75.0; older versions have different cache/timing conditions.
rcloneCases.verdict: Not a demonstrated v1.74.3 exploit yet, but its source has the username-global password map, per-operation lookup and username-only credential-checked cache. After cache expiry an accepted replacement credential can still rebind the older session; no source-based nonapplicability established.
rcloneCases.sourceOrConfigurationRemediation: Bind credentials to the FTP session. A bounded loopback test on authenticated shipped bytes with explicit cache expiry would establish the older-version boundary; absent immediate reproduction is not proof of safety.

rcloneNewPublisherSourceLead.verdict: Real potential partial remediation of seven rclone main-module findings and embedded module floors; not yet a compatible approved package/source or stdlib clearance.
rcloneNewPublisherSourceLead.existingPublisherRoute: Fedora-signed owning update/backport/rebuild; do not repeat unchanged availability query until publication event.
rcloneNewPublisherSourceLead.newOfficialPublisherRoute: Requires explicit source/trust review and actual compatible RPM transaction/binary module proof; do not silently substitute an unsigned archive or overwrite RPM files.

codeShellQuote.verdict: Strong source-level false-positive lead; not granted because exact shipped Code runtime files and all runtime importers remain unbound.
codeShellQuote.condition: quote() must receive an actual object comment token before a later attacker-controlled string with a line terminator in the same token array. parse-only callers and arrays containing strings only cannot produce this specific comment-token boundary.

exactCodeSource.otherLockConsumer: npm-run-all2 is a devDependency in this exact Code package.json; do not assume installed exclusion without bundle proof.

onlyDirectShellQuoteImports.quoteCallerRoles: String paths/env/argv, shell -c string argument, inner script string, bwrap string argv; no parse() or object comment token construction observed in published runtime.
String environment entries, sandbox-exec argv and command strings. Not used as a Linux platform exclusion for the shared module.

Argument construction and input validation must be covered in final source review; dynamic importers, other packages and actual Microsoft bundle differences remain unknown.

Include all current native/retained package locations. If all are string-only or parser-only, propose exact digest/component/alias/path nonapplicability; otherwise request Microsoft-signed1.11-containing Code update.

httpConditionalClassification.mechanism: An HTTP/1 CONNECT request with nonempty body, non-2xx keep-alive rejection and pooled reuse can poison the response consumed by a later caller. Cross-user impact requires a shared transport boundary such as a reverse proxy.
httpConditionalClassification.classification: Conditional client/forwarder risk; ordinary TLS proxy CONNECT with no Request.Body is not this mechanism.
httpConditionalClassification.positiveProofRequired: Enumerate every supported CONNECT-producing caller, Body assignment, rejection behavior and shared transport reuse; exact compiled source/bytes at all native locations. Client-only labeling or absent CONNECT symbols is insufficient.

httpConditionalClassification.mechanism: An HTTP/2 client accepts malformed framing headers; response smuggling requires forwarding those headers to a lenient HTTP/1 peer when acting as a reverse proxy.
httpConditionalClassification.classification: Official description does not establish desktop takeover for a terminal client that consumes the response without forwarding it. Such clients are high-yield nonapplicability leads, not accepted scopes yet.
httpConditionalClassification.positiveProofRequired: Trace each supported HTTP/2 response consumer and every serialization/header-forwarding path; prove there is no lenient downstream HTTP/1 boundary, including optional servers and proxy roles. stdlib and x/net copies require distinct exact-component coverage.

httpConditionalClassification.mechanism: An HTTP/1 handler returns a successful CONNECT response without hijacking the connection, while an intermediate peer treats it as a tunnel. The server continues parsing HTTP and can disagree with the proxy boundary.
httpConditionalClassification.classification: Conditional server/proxy risk; importing net/http or running a client does not establish this handler path.
httpConditionalClassification.positiveProofRequired: Inventory every supported HTTP/1 server handler, CONNECT method response, default/fallback route and Hijack behavior. Prove CONNECT rejects before success, or prove safe hijack/closure; exact compiled source/binary/module/location binding remains required.

recommendedSequence: First bind the exact current Code sandbox files/importers; the positive string-only published caller shape is the strongest cheap new false-positive lead.
Continue root Go CONNECT/reverse-proxy source role proof with the explicit advisory conditions; never infer vulnerability or nonapplicability merely from net/http symbols.

Keep AnyIO and supported rclone client/server paths blocked until owning signed fixes/backports or complete enforced/applicability evidence. Source fixes now exist upstream; approved package publication remains a separate dependency.

If product scope changes are desired, ask for explicit decisions on individual server/remote-hash/link functionality or optional packages after dependency proof; removing server support alone cannot clear rclone client --links and remote PowerShell risks.
Only when new source fixes or complete exact-digest proofs change evidence, reuse retained results for review and scan a changed candidate once; signing and boot gates remain separate.
